speaker: Doctor
text: I need to understand the onset of your symptoms: did the fever and wrist pain start at the same time, and what do the skin lesions look like? Also, have you had any recent insect bites or traveled to a specific location recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Lyme Disease (Erythema Migrans with monoarticular arthritis). The history of Minnesota camping, recent knee pain, and current wrist pain with systemic symptoms is classic for early disseminated Lyme disease, though a localized skin rash (Erythema Migrans) at the bite site or the specific appearance of the wrist lesion needs confirmation. REQUEST TEST: Lyme_Serology (ELISA and Western Blot); REQUEST IMAGES: Photos of the wrist lesion and knee.
